artists.biography:
Purson are a psychedelic rock band from London, England. Founded by Rosalie Cunningham, currently signed to Rise Above Records. Purson formed after Cunningham disbanded her previous project Ipso Facto (band).

Purson appeared at the 2012 edition of Roadburn Festival.

The band performed live in session for Marc Riley on BBC Radio 6 Music in January 2012 and again in March 2013. Purson have performed alongside label mates Uncle Acid & the Deadbeats, Electric Wizard , Blood Ceremony, Comus (band), Pentagram (band) as well as Neo-psychedelia bands such as Toy and Temples.

Their first single Rocking Horse was released on the 1st of March 2012.

Purson's debut album titled The Circle And The Blue Door was Released on 29 April 2013 to general and critical acclaim.

Spin called the album "an audacious entry into a current crop of retro-pop headbanger fare that should chill the marrow of fans".

Virgin wrote "Long before the last track has played its final note you will already be planning your next visit to this dark yet enchanting musical world. ‘The Circle & The Blue Door‘ is thoroughly addictive listening".

The Circle And The Blue Door ranked number 4 on About.com's best heavy Metal Albums of April 2013.

perplexity.description:
Purson’s Desire's Magic Theatre, released in 2016 on Spinefarm Records, is a vibrant and ambitious album that stands as the band’s sophomore full-length effort. Musically, the album blends psychedelic rock, classic rock, and progressive elements, drawing clear inspiration from the 1960s and 1970s while maintaining a fresh and contemporary sound. The record is noted for its dynamic songwriting, colorful arrangements, and a seamless fusion of vintage and modern influences, with tracks like the title opener and “Electric Landlady” showcasing the band’s ability to balance melodic psychedelia with heavier, more energetic moments.

Within Purson’s discography, Desire's Magic Theatre marks a significant evolution, demonstrating the band’s growth without sacrificing their core identity. Critics praised the album for its ability to honor the psychedelic traditions of the past while pushing the genre forward, with many highlighting its inventive production and strong performances. The album received positive reviews for its originality and depth, with outlets describing it as a “timeless psychedelic rock masterpiece” and commending its ability to both surprise and satisfy fans of classic rock and progressive music.
